about.title: Yorba Linda Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Yorba Linda is a city of about 67,973 people, and nearly every home in it depends on products that someone else designed, built, and sold: the ladder used to clean gutters, the car seat buckled in for the drive down Imperial Highway, the charger left plugged in overnight. Most of those products work. When one fails and hurts someone, California law takes a distinct approach. Product liability claims usually rest on strict liability, which means you generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. You need to show the product had a defect, whether in its design, in how a particular unit was made, or in the warnings that came with it, and that the defect caused your injury. Responsibility can reach the manufacturer, the distributor, and the Orange County retailer that sold it. What matters most right away is keeping the product, its packaging, and any receipts exactly as they are. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, and we connect Yorba Linda residents with an independent attorney who handles these claims on contingency.

items.title: Strict Liability Means a Different Kind of Case
items.desc: In California, you generally do not have to prove a manufacturer was negligent, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. The attorneys in our network understand how to build a claim around that standard.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving the Product
items.desc: The defective item is usually the single most important piece of evidence. An attorney can explain how to keep it, its packaging, and its documentation intact before anything is discarded or returned.

items.title: Every Link in the Chain Is Considered
items.desc: Liability can extend beyond the manufacturer to distributors and the retailer who sold the product in Orange County. The attorney you are connected with can identify each party that may be responsible.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash on Yorba Linda Boulevard and I think my airbag never deployed. Is that a product claim?
items.answer: It might be. Yorba Linda recorded 91 injury collisions in 2025, and in some crashes the injuries are made worse by a vehicle part that did not perform as designed, such as an airbag, a seatbelt, or a tire. A claim against another driver and a product liability claim against the part's maker can exist side by side. Do not have the vehicle repaired or scrapped until an attorney has advised you.

items.question: What if I already threw the product away?
items.answer: Contact an attorney anyway. Photos, the box, the receipt, an online order record, or even the same model still on a store shelf can help establish what the product was and how it failed. If any part of the item remains, stop using it and set it aside as is.

items.question: Does it cost anything to be connected with an attorney, and what will the attorney charge?
items.answer: LawProactive is free to use, and we are not a law firm. The independent attorneys we connect Yorba Linda residents with work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery in your case. The attorney will explain the specific terms before you agree to anything.
